module_title: DPSP - Ideological Classification and Key Articles
introduction: Although the Constitution does not formally classify the Directive Principles, based on their content and direction, they are generally classified into three categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles. At this level, we will memorize the most frequently tested articles.

core_concepts.title: Gandhian Principles
core_concepts.description: Based on Gandhi's vision of village swaraj and upliftment. Art 40: Organization of village panchayats. Art 43: Promote cottage industries in rural areas. Art 47: Prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs. Art 48: Prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch cattle.

core_concepts.title: Socialistic Principles
core_concepts.description: Aimed at providing socio-economic justice. Art 39(b) & (c): Prevention of concentration of wealth and equitable distribution of material resources. Art 41: Right to work, education, and public assistance. Art 42: Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

core_concepts.title: Liberal-Intellectual Principles
core_concepts.description: Art 44: Secure a 'Uniform Civil Code' (UCC) for all citizens. Art 45: Early childhood care and education for all children until they complete 6 years of age. Art 50: Separation of the judiciary from the executive. Art 51: Promote international peace and security.

important_entities.name: K.T. Shah
important_entities.significance: He criticized the non-justiciable nature of DPSPs, famously calling it 'a cheque on a bank, payable only when the resources of the bank permit'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Originally, Article 45 provided for free education up to 14 years. The 86th Amendment (2002) elevated education for 6-14 year olds to a Fundamental Right (Art 21A) and altered the subject matter of Art 45 to 'early childhood care' for children between 0 to 6 years.
Note that the UCC is not implemented throughout India. For a long time, it was applicable only in Goa, and recently Uttarakhand became the first state to pass a UCC bill post-independence.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Art 40 (Panchayat), Art 44 (Uniform Civil Code - the digits 4 and 4 are uniform), Art 50 (Separation of Judiciary & Executive - 50/50 split).

exam_strategy_tips: Match the following questions pairing 'Articles' with their 'Provisions' are highly common, especially for Articles 40, 44, 48, 50, and 51.
Which article forms the basis of India's foreign policy? (Answer: Article 51).
